blocks.text: How can I find the equation of a perpendicular bisector?

blocks.md:
- The **perpendicular bisector** of a line segment:

  - is perpendicular to the line segment
  - goes through the midpoint of the line segment

blocks.alt: Perpendicular Bisector, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - The midpoint and gradient of the line segment between points **(*****x***<sub>**1**</sub>**, *****y***<sub>**1**</sub>**)** and **(*****x***<sub>**2**</sub>**, *****y***<sub>**2**</sub>**)** are given by the formulae

blocks.alt: Midpoint Gradient Forms, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - The gradient of the perpendicular bisector is therefore

blocks.alt: Perp Bisector Gradient, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - The equation of the perpendicular bisector is the equation of the line with that gradient through the line segment's midpoint (see Equation of a Straight Line)

blocks.text: How can I use perpendicular bisectors to find the equation of a circle?

blocks.md: - A **chord** of a circle is a straight line segment between any two points on the circle

blocks.alt: Chord, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - The perpendicular bisector of a chord always goes through the centre of the circle

blocks.alt: Perp Bisect Chord, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - If you know three points on a circle, draw any two chords between them – the perpendicular bisectors of the chords will meet at the centre of the circle

blocks.alt: Perp Bisect Centre, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - Now that you know the centre of the circle and a point on the circle you can write the equation of the circle
